questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to the US to experience college life, and how the universities function in a different way than in Europe. Boston is a city with a lot of students, good universities, a lot of history and i therefore chose to go to Boston.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get a BU email account. they send you everything you need, even though they sometimes spam you a little bit too much, so you kind of have to search for the relevant information:)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: BU students were there to take care of me, which was a great help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: they had an orientiation program, be sure to be there for that, as you get to meet all the other exchange students here

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I applied for dorms, but BU currently have a housing crisis and do not have enough dorms which meant i lived on the Hyatt Hotel in Cambridge with all the other exchange students. This was a huge upgrade, as the dorms are quite shitty. BU secure housing for you, which was a huge plus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: they have a bunch of different meal plans, which are really good. if you live on campus you must have a meal plan, but i can recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be happy if you get the Hyatt Hotel its much better than the dorms and cost the same. there is a shuttle bus to campus every 15 minutes, but you can also walk there in 15 minutes.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: sign up as soon as possible to get the courses you want, and if they are full, email the instructors and ask if they have space for you even though its full - it works.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: sign up for the courses and do not go on the wait list of wait. you can drop courses later if you do not want them, so make sure to sign up early, to make sure you are in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not much until at orentiation.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do it as soon as possible and sign up, you can drop the courses later on, if you do not want them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: take as many courses as possible at the BU Pardee school (IR School) - it is much better and with better professors than the Political Science department.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300- level courses are very easy. 400- is suitable. 500- is quite hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: smaller classes, you get to know the professors, so take the chance and connect with them. you have to participate a little bit, so it reminds me of a danish high school just with a higher level of teaching. also bigger workload, as you have midterms, quizzes and presentations along the semester, instead of just one exam at the end like back at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CASPO 343: Europe and International Relations (EP), CASPO 344: Democracy, Origins and Breakdown (DAK3), CASIR 428: International Negotiations (Valgfag), COMCM 531: International Communication (Valgfag).

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
TAKE CASIR 428 WITH PROFESSOR -NAME REDACTED- - BEST COURSE I HAVE EVER HAD.

If you´re interested in IR, diplomacy and international negotiations, then this course is a must!. -NAME REDACTED-  is a former american ambassador, and teaches how diplomacy unfolds in practice. You have excercises in class, where you train your negotiation skills, which makes the course interactive and super fun. The professor is very inspiring, so i cannot stress how much you should take this course, and all other courses he offers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa - expect a fee of approximately 3,000 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and meal plan are super expensive, as well as insurance. But when you have it and you have paid, you live realtively cheap, as everything is "paid for" already.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: a lot of clubs - go to SPLASH to view all of them. for sports go to ice hockey as BU is top 5 school in ice hockey in the US. For American Football go to BC!! and Patriots. For Basketball go to Celtics and for Baseball Red Sox. Boston has got the best sports teams of the US in almost every sport.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go hiking in white mountains. go to new york. explore new england area in general, and go to the countryside, its like a different world out there, and people are so different to the Bostonians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Watch sports all you can. Have a real thanksgiving experience, so get an american friend to invite you home. in the beginning of the semester, when the workload is low, go on a lot of trips, experience Boston and New England, NYC, etc. Later on in the semester you will not have as much time to do all that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy - Boston is the most "European" city in the US.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be open, americans love to talk, so yap as much as possible

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the hospitality. i got invited home to thanksgiving with an american family, and 3 other people, even my professor also asked me to celebrate thanksgiving with them. Americans are super kind, and hospitable, so take the chance and experience that!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. dont be scared of trump and visas - it will work out. 
2. go to orientation - you meet other exchange students here
3. have a blast

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the people you meet

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the workload is much higher than UCPH. you become tired in exam periods on another level

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
